[I treat this as a common-value, second-price auction. Signal s=44 implies true common value C must lie in [s-20, s+20]∩[20,29] = [24,29]. With a uniform prior/likelihood the posterior on C is uniform on [24,29], so E[C|s]=26.5. In a second-price auction the Bayes-Nash strategy is to bid your posterior expected common value to avoid the winner’s curse and maximize expected profit. ]
